abstract: Norovirus (NoV), a major global acute gastroenteritis pathogen, has high genetic diversity. Developing precise, rapid typing methods is crucial for epidemic control and vaccine development. Thus, this study develops a machine learning tool based on Norovirus genomic k-mer (length-k nucleotide fragments) features. It enables rapid, accurate dual-region typing of RdRp (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) and VP1 (major capsid protein) without alignment or segmentation. Using k-mer frequency features with k = 11, the MurmurHash3 algorithm maps the features to a 2²⁰-dimensional space and constructs a hash feature table. A random forest model comprising 500 decision trees is then used. Each tree randomly selects 20 features during node splitting. The model is trained and evaluated using a bootstrap sampling strategy (80% training and 20% out-of-bag estimation), and prediction confidence intervals are outputted. The typing accuracy rates for the RdRp region and VP1 region reached 97.6% and 99.3%, respectively. Analysis of precision, recall, and F1-score for each genotype in the test set showed that all metrics for the 40 RdRp genotypes and 34 VP1 genotypes were ≥ 0.9. Typing accuracy across all length intervals was ≥ 0.96. This study integrates machine learning and bioinformatics to develop a novel norovirus genome analysis tool. It enables precise genotyping despite multi-region interference and reveals hidden genomic information, supporting viral classification and tracing. The feature hashing and ensemble learning strategies overcome traditional dependencies on alignment and annotation, offering a universal, efficient, scalable framework for viral genome identification.

title: Construction of a machine learning model for dual-region typing of norovirus RdRp and VP1 based on genomic k-mer features.
